description: We are students at El-Dabaa Nuclear School, home to Egypt’s first nuclear power program. Growing up beside this national project taught us that big ideas need rigorous science, careful engineering, and a deep sense of responsibility. We’re here to apply that mindset to NASA’s challenges, using Earth observation data to build solutions that serve people and the planet.
summary: Dawra is a free web tool that helps farmers explore crop-rotation options. A farmer enters their current three-season rotation and what matters most (water, soil, income, heat tolerance). Dawra compares it with the best one-crop changes and with a fully new rotation, and explains each option with evidence, information gaps and risks that need local review. It addresses the challenge by turning NASA climate data and crop traits into a clear, farmer-friendly comparison that supports farmers' judgment rather than replacing it. It matters because heat, uneven rainfall and water limits make rotation choices harder, and wrong choices can drain soil and use more water.
details:
What it does: The user picks a starting season, enters the current three-season rotation (for example wheat > rice > wheat) and sets four priority sliders (water, soil, income, heat tolerance). An optional scenario slider adds up to +4 C and changes rainfall from -40% to +20%. Dawra scores the current rotation, shows the two best one-crop changes and the best full rotation for that season. Each card lists benefits, evidence from the data, information gaps, risks for local review, an estimate of bare-field days, and a stability check (does the option stay among the best when priorities change?).

How it works: Scores combine four indicators: water, soil, heat and income. Water uses crop water need and a rainfall-based stress index. Heat uses days with a daily maximum of 35 C or more. Soil rewards legumes after cereals, plant-family diversity and alternating root depth. Rotations that repeat a crop or plant family back to back, or put a high-water crop after rice, lose 10 points per violation. All calculations run in the browser.

Benefits and goals: farmers can compare their rotation with simple alternatives, see why each is suggested and where information is missing. The tool is a decision aid, not a yield forecast, and it does not replace local agronomists.

Pilot area: Tanta, Nile Delta (30.7865 N, 31.0004 E). Scores use 2025 data. [A 2005-2025 yearly series is shown for long-term context.]

Known limits (stated in the tool): one point; scores are indicative; irrigation water is not measured; bare-field days are estimated from crop duration, not from satellite NDVI; NDVI is not integrated; soil values are historical (1995-96); water, heat and income indices per crop are team estimates.

Tools: React 18, Vite 5, JavaScript, HTML/CSS (web app, no hardware); Python for data preparation; hosted on Vercel. Live site: https://dawra-nasa-2026.vercel.app
